o: Merge weight sums by value across two item lists and output sorted by value. Values are unique within each list but may overlap across lists; values and weights are at most 1000, so a 1001-slot accumulation array plus a sort (or direct in-order scan) solves it instantly.
k: Accumulate weights per value in one dictionary/array from both lists.
Output must be sorted ascending by value — sort the keys or scan a bounded array in order.
Values are unique within each input list, so simple addition cannot double-count.

a.i: Add every (value, weight) into a shared map, then emit (value, totalWeight) pairs sorted by value. With values <= 1000, a fixed-size array and an in-order scan avoids sorting entirely.
s: Create an array/dict indexed by value.
Add weights from items1 and items2.
Collect entries with nonzero weight in ascending value order.
a.t: O(n log n) with a hash map + sort, or O(n + V) with the bounded array scan (V = 1000).

w: Straightforward; the only mistakes possible are forgetting the ascending-order requirement or merging into separate maps. Follow-up: merge k item lists, or support value ranges/deletion queries with a balanced BST.
